A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DFlash work. All main-text and appendix pages are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding speedups, throughput, acceptance lengths and ablation results, including the appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds long-context adaptation, conditioning ablations, additional model comparisons and vLLM measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed parallel block-diffusion drafting, per-layer KV conditioning, random-anchor training and loss weighting remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 documents the existing mechanism more precisely; the added autoregressive and input-fusion variants serve as experimental controls.

E1.justification: Section 5.4 adds training on LongAlign-10K and evaluation on LongBench's hotpotqa, qasper and gov_report datasets. This substantially extends the retained coverage to long-context scenarios, reaching 16K context for all three datasets and 32K for gov_report.

E2.justification: The original autoregressive and EAGLE-3 comparisons remain. Table 11 adds native MTP comparisons on three Qwen3.5 models, while Table 9 introduces EAGLE-3-5L, DFlash-AR and input-fusion/KV conditioning comparisons, substantially expanding the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: New protocols include fine-tuning Qwen3.5-27B's drafter on 1.6K samples for three epochs, context-length sweeps, and conditioning controls with five draft layers and block size eight. Appendix A.4 adds Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Coder-Next and GPT-OSS configurations, SGLang evaluations at concurrency eight, and vLLM evaluations at concurrency 1, 8, 16 and 32. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.5.5 adds a controlled comparison of KV injection versus input fusion under both autoregressive and diffusion drafting. Section 5.4 newly tests long-context degradation and recovery through fine-tuning. These address distinct mechanism and robustness questions beyond the retained depth, feature-count, block-size, loss-decay and anchor-sampling ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its results. The added experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All nine original result tables retain their values after renumbering, and the original plotted results are unchanged. New Tables 4, 9, 11 and 12 substantially expand the findings. For example, v2 reports hotpotqa acceptance lengths of 3.61 versus 6.05 for base versus adapted drafters at 16K, and Qwen3.5-9B Math500 speedups of 1.7× for MTP versus 3.5× for DFlash. These are added experiments, not revised original scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the fused target features and layerwise Q/K/V construction, together with a parameter-memory calculation. This is a limited addition to the mathematical specification; the existing speedup analysis and loss-weight formula remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: lightweight diffusion drafting conditioned on target features enables fast, lossless speculative decoding. The headline claims of over 6× acceleration and up to 2.5× higher speedup than EAGLE-3 are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that lightweight adaptation preserves useful target-feature conditioning at longer contexts and that KV conditioning and parallel drafting make distinct contributions to speed. Appendix A.3 also argues that the additional projection and activation costs are modest. Existing interpretations and deployment tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly specifies the shared RMSNorm projection, Q/K/V construction, bypassed computation and example memory requirements. The new experiments disclose fine-tuning sample and epoch counts and additional serving configurations. The original training recipe and code/model links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for LongAlign, LongBench, vLLM/PagedAttention and the GPT-OSS model card. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to EAGLE, PARD and diffusion-based speculative decoding remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained. v2 adds focused experimental and appendix subsections, broadens the serving-section title, and adds conflict-of-interest and impact statements. Acknowledgements, publication text and cross-references receive limited updates.

P2.justification: New Tables 4, 9, 11 and 12 introduce substantial displays for context adaptation, conditioning controls, MTP/model comparisons and vLLM concurrency. Existing tables are retained but renumbered and repositioned. All five original figures remain, with Figure 5 relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: v1's conditioning argument relied on indirect depth and no-feature ablations; v2's matched-depth conditioning comparison directly strengthens the explanation of DFlash's advantage. Long-context adaptation tests, native-MTP comparisons and vLLM results substantially strengthen evidence for practical applicability, while Appendix A.3 clarifies the central mechanism and its costs. These gains improve validation and technical transparency without removing prior evidence, although uncertainty across runs remains unreported.
